Summary: Create an issue

Any user with pull access to a repository can create an issue. If [issues are disabled in the repository](https://docs.github.com/articles/disabling-issues/), the API returns a `410 Gone` status.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

Parameters:

  - repo (path, string, required): The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

Possible response status codes: 201, 400, 403, 404, 410, 422, 503

(Create an issue)

  - body (optional), type: string: The contents of the issue.
  - assignee (optional), type: string: Login for the user that this issue should be assigned to. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set the assignee for new issues. The assignee is silently dropped otherwise. **This field is closing do
  - milestone (optional), type: string: 
  - labels (optional), type: array: Labels to associate with this issue. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set labels for new issues. Labels are silently dropped otherwise._
  - assignees (optional), type: array: Logins for Users to assign to this issue. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set assignees for new issues. Assignees are silently dropped otherwise._
  - issue_field_values (optional), type: array: An array of issue field values to set on this issue. Each field value must include the field ID and the value to set. Issue fields are only available for organization-owned repositories with the featu

response:
To create a new issue, send a **POST** request to the repository’s issues endpoint:

```
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues
```

- Any user with pull access to the repository can create an issue [cite: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues].
- The request body must include the required field `title` [cite: Request body schema for POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues].
- Optional fields you can include are `body`, `assignee`, `milestone`, `labels`, `assignees`, `issue_field_values`, and `type` [cite: Request body schema for POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues].
- On success the API returns **201 Created** [cite: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues].
- If the repository has issues disabled, the API returns **410 Gone** [cite: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues].
- You can request different media types (`raw`, `text`, `html`, `full`) to receive the body in various formats [cite: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues].

**Example request body**

```json
{
  "title": "Bug: login fails on Safari",
  "body": "Steps to reproduce:\n1. Open Safari\n2. ...",
  "labels": ["bug", "high priority"]
}
```

Send this payload to the endpoint with the appropriate `owner` and `repo` path parameters to create the issue.

Summary: Check if a pull request has been merged

Checks if a pull request has been merged into the base branch. The HTTP status of the response indicates whether or not the pull request has been merged; the response body is empty.

Parameters:
  - owner (path, string, required): The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

response:
To merge a pull request with the GitHub REST API, send a **PUT** request to

```
/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge
```

Replace `{owner}`, `{repo}`, and `{pull_number}` with the repository owner, repository name, and pull‑request number, respectively. 
The request body can include any of the following optional fields:

* `commit_title` – string, title for the automatic commit message. 
* `commit_message` – string, extra detail to append to the automatic commit message. 
* `sha` – string, SHA that the pull‑request head must match to allow the merge. 
* `merge_method` – string, the merge method to use. 

The endpoint returns one of the following status codes: 200 (merged), 403, 404, 405, 409, or 422. 
A successful merge triggers notifications. 

After merging, you can verify the merge status with a **GET** request to the same URL; a 204 status means the pull request has been merged, while 404 means it has not.

POST /repos/{template_owner}/{template_repo}/generate
Summary: Create a repository using a template

Creates a new repository using a repository template. Use the `template_owner` and `template_repo` route parameters to specify the repository to use as the template. If the repository is not public, the authenticated user must own or be a member of an organization that owns the repository. To check if a repository is available to use as a template, get the repository's information using the [Get a repository](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository) endpoint and check that the `is_template` key is `true`.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `public_repo` or `repo` scope to create a public repository, and `repo` scope to create a private repository.

Parameters:
  - template_owner (path, string, required): The account owner of the template repository. The name is not case sensitive.
  - template_repo (path, string, required): The name of the template repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

Possible response status codes: 201

Request body schema for POST /repos/{template_owner}/{template_repo}/generate
(Create a repository using a template)

Required fields: name

Fields:
  - owner (optional), type: string: The organization or person who will own the new repository. To create a new repository in an organization, the authenticated user must be a member of the specified organization.
  - name (required), type: string: The name of the new repository.
  - description (optional), type: string: A short description of the new repository.
  - include_all_branches (optional), type: boolean: Set to `true` to include the directory structure and files from all branches in the template repository, and not just the default branch. Default: `false`.
  - private (optional), type: boolean: Either `true` to create a new private repository or `false` to create a new public one.
response:
To create a repository inside an organization, send a **POST** request to 
`/repos/{template_owner}/{template_repo}/generate` and include the organization’s name in the `owner` field of the request body. The authenticated user must be a member of that organization, and the token must have the `repo` scope (or `public_repo` for public repos) to create the repository. 

- `owner` (optional) – set to the organization name to own the new repo . 
- User must be a member of the organization to create a repo there . 
- Token scopes: `public_repo` or `repo` for public repos, `repo` for private repos .
reference: Send a POST request to /orgs/{org}/repos with at least the 'name' field.

(Create a repository using a template)

Required fields: name

Fields:

To create a new repository from a template:

1. Send a **POST** request to  
   `/repos/{template_owner}/{template_repo}/generate`  
   where `{template_owner}` is the account that owns the template and `{template_repo}` is the template repository name.  
   [cite: POST /repos/{template_owner}/{template_repo}/generate]

2. Include a JSON body that contains at least the required field `name` (the new repository’s name).  
   Optional fields you can add are `owner`, `description`, `include_all_branches`, and `private`.  
   [cite: Request body schema for POST /repos/{template_owner}/{template_repo}/generate]

3. Authenticate with an OAuth app token or a classic personal access token that has the `public_repo` or `repo` scope (for public repositories) or `repo` scope (for private repositories).

Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{

  "description": "Created from template",
  "private": false,
  "include_all_branches": true
}

## About validating webhook deliveries

Once your server is configured to receive payloads, it will listen for any delivery that's sent to the endpoint you configured. To ensure that your server only processes webhook deliveries that were sent by  and to ensure that the delivery was not tampered with, you should validate the webhook signature before processing the delivery further. This will help you avoid spending server time to process deliveries that are not from  and will help avoid man-in-the-middle attacks.

To do this, you need to:

1. Create a secret token for a webhook.
1. Store the token securely on your server.
1. Validate incoming webhook payloads against the token, to verify that they are coming from  and were not tampered with.

Validating webhook deliveries — Creating a secret token

You can create a new webhook with a secret token, or you can add a secret token to an existing webhook. When creating a secret token, you should choose a random string of text with high entropy.

* _To create a new webhook with a secret token_, see (see: /webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks).
* _To add a secret token to an existing webhook_, edit the webhook's settings. Under "Secret", type a string to use as a `secret` key. For more information, see (see: /webhooks/using-webhooks/editing-webhooks).

Validating webhook deliveries — Securely storing the secret token

After creating a secret token, you should store it in a secure location that your server can access. Never hardcode a token into an application or push a token to any repository. For more information about how to use authentication credentials securely in your code, see (see: /rest/authentication/keeping-your-api-credentials-secure#use-authentication-credentials-securely-in-your-code).

You can provide an additional `committer` parameter, which is an object containing information about the committer. Or, you can provide an `author` parameter, which is an object containing information about the author.

The `author` section is optional and is filled in with the `committer` information if omitted. If the `committer` information is omitted, the authenticated user's information is used.

You must provide values for both `name` and `email`, whether you choose to use `author` or `committer`. Otherwise, you'll receive a `422` status code.

> [!NOTE]
> If you use this endpoint and the "[Create or update file contents](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/contents/#create-or-update-file-contents)" endpoint in parallel, the concurrent requests will conflict and you will receive errors. You must use these endpoints serially instead.
